## Independent project entries

| Project | What it does | Best starting point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [initx](/projects/initx/) | Runs developer scripts through installable plugins. | [Install and run a plugin](/projects/initx/getting-started) |

## How to use this site

Each project is documented independently. Its pages cover the overview, setup, architecture, reference, constraints, and troubleshooting:

1. **Overview** gives the direct answer: what the project is, who it is for, and what it intentionally does not do.
2. **Getting started** contains copyable install and first-run commands.
3. **Architecture** explains the runtime boundary and the important design decisions.
4. **Reference** records commands, flags, inputs, outputs, and compatibility facts.
5. **Constraints and troubleshooting** explain security, failure paths, and recovery steps.
6. **FAQ** resolves common intent and edge cases in short, quotable answers.

The default language is English. Chinese translations live under [`/zh/`](/zh/), with the same route structure. Machine readers can use [`llms.txt`](/llms.txt), [`llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt), [`summary.json`](/summary.json), and [`sitemap.xml`](/sitemap.xml).

<p class="source-note">Project facts are derived from the local repositories and their public package metadata. Exact commands belong to the project repositories linked from each page.</p>

The person behind these projects is described on the [author page](/about).

## What I build

The projects on this site cover several independent areas:

- Developer CLIs and release tools such as [initx](/projects/initx/) and [cargo-bumpp](/projects/cargo-bumpp/).
- Browser extensions and local-first applications such as [Mail Peon](/projects/mail-peon/) and [Offer Hunter](/projects/offer-hunter/).
- Language, parser, and editor tooling such as [yyds-lang](/projects/yyds-lang/) and [bigseek](/projects/bigseek/).
- Developer infrastructure, build plugins, and runtime utilities such as [flash-tunnel](/projects/flash-tunnel/), [ext-kit](/projects/ext-kit/), and [unplugin-build-stamp](/projects/unplugin-build-stamp/).

Each project has its own scope, repository, runtime boundary, and documentation set. The author relationship identifies who maintains or explores the project; it does not merge the projects into one product.

## Source and maintenance

The canonical implementation for each project is its linked GitHub repository. This site adds a stable, bilingual, citation-friendly explanation around those repositories and generates machine-readable project indexes from the Markdown source.

For the complete project list, open the [projects directory](/projects/). For public activity and repository ownership, use the [GitHub profile](https://github.com/imba97).

# How this GEO index works

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/guide/geo/
Language: en
Project: site
Description: Learn how the VitePress site exposes project facts to people, search engines, and language models through structured pages and generated files.

# How this GEO index works

This site is a VitePress documentation root with English as the default language and a mirrored Chinese tree under `/zh/`. Its page structure is designed around answerable intents: what a project is, how to start it, how it works, and where its boundaries are.

## Page-level signals

- Each page has a concise `title` and `description` in frontmatter.
- The build adds canonical URLs, `hreflang` links, Open Graph metadata, and JSON-LD (`WebSite` for site pages and `TechArticle` for project pages).
- Project pages expose exact commands, versions, runtime boundaries, privacy statements, and explicit non-goals.
- English and Chinese pages keep the same information architecture so a crawler can map translations reliably.

## Generated discovery files

`pnpm generate:geo` runs the TypeScript generator through `esno`, scans the Markdown tree, and writes these files to `docs/public/`:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `llms.txt` | Short, linked map of projects and pages. |
| `/projects/<id>/llms.txt` | Independent machine-readable index for one project, including its English and Chinese pages. |
| `llms-full.txt` | Full Markdown content with URL, language, project, and description metadata. |
| `summary.json` | Structured site, project, page, language, and feed metadata. |
| `sitemap.xml` | All English and Chinese routes with a build timestamp. |
| `robots.txt` | Allows crawling and points to the sitemap. |

The two plain-text LLM files are written as UTF-8 with a BOM and are served with an explicit `charset=utf-8` header so browsers and text viewers do not fall back to a legacy encoding.

Set `SITE_URL` during deployment when the canonical hostname changes. The default is `https://projects.imba97.dev`.

Use `pnpm check:geo` in CI to verify that every source page is represented in the existing summary and `llms.txt` files without rewriting them.

## Content contract for new projects

Add a project with an overview, getting-started page, architecture page, reference page, constraints/security page, troubleshooting page, and FAQ in both language trees. Add project-specific decision, integration, or operations pages when the source repository contains enough facts to support them. Give every page a direct first paragraph, a single primary intent, a stable canonical route, and links to the source repository. Then run `pnpm generate:geo` and `pnpm build`.

# 这套 GEO 索引如何工作

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/guide/geo/
Language: zh-CN
Project: site
Description: 了解 VitePress 文档站如何通过双语页面、结构化元数据和自动生成文件服务搜索引擎与语言模型。

# 这套 GEO 索引如何工作

这是一个以 VitePress 为根站点的文档索引，英文默认，中文统一放在 `/zh/`。页面围绕可回答的搜索意图组织：项目是什么、如何开始、如何运行、边界在哪里。

## 页面信号

- 每页 frontmatter 都有简洁的 `title` 与 `description`。
- 构建时注入 canonical、`hreflang`、Open Graph 和 JSON-LD；项目页使用 `TechArticle`，站点页使用 `WebSite`。
- 项目页面写明可复制命令、版本要求、运行边界、隐私与明确不做的事情。
- 中英文保持相同信息架构，爬虫可以稳定匹配翻译页。

## 自动生成入口

执行 `pnpm generate:geo` 会通过 `esno` 运行 TypeScript 生成器，扫描 Markdown 并写入 `docs/public/`：

| 文件 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `llms.txt` | 项目与页面的短索引。 |
| `/projects/<id>/llms.txt` | 单个项目的独立机器索引，包含该项目的中英文页面。 |
| `llms-full.txt` | 带 URL、语言、项目和描述的完整 Markdown。 |
| `summary.json` | 结构化站点、项目、页面和 feed 元数据。 |
| `sitemap.xml` | 全部中英文路由。 |
| `robots.txt` | 允许抓取并指向 sitemap。 |

两个纯文本 LLM 文件会以带 BOM 的 UTF-8 写入，并通过显式的 `charset=utf-8` 响应头提供，避免浏览器或文本查看器误用旧编码。

部署时可以设置 `SITE_URL` 覆盖 canonical 域名，默认是 `https://projects.imba97.dev`。

CI 中可以执行 `pnpm check:geo`，校验现有 `summary.json` 和 `llms.txt` 是否覆盖所有源页面，且不会改写生成文件。

## 新增项目的内容约定

中英文各增加项目总览、快速开始、架构、参考手册、约束/安全、故障排查和 FAQ；如果源仓库有足够事实，再增加项目自己的设计决策、集成或运维页面。每页首段直接回答一个主要问题，给出稳定 canonical 路由，并链接到源仓库。完成后执行 `pnpm generate:geo` 与 `pnpm build`。

## Project: initx

# initx — plugin-powered scripting engine

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: initx is a Node.js CLI that turns repeatable developer tasks into installable plugins, with initx and ix command aliases.

# initx

<p class="lead"><code>initx</code> is a plugin-powered scripting engine for developer workflows. Install the CLI, add a plugin, and replace a multi-step shell recipe with a short command. The package also exposes <code>ix</code> as a compact alias.</p>

Maintainer: [imba97](/about).

## What problem does initx solve?

initx keeps small operational scripts discoverable and composable. The core CLI handles command dispatch and plugin installation; plugins own the task-specific behavior. This lets a workflow such as setting Git identity, copying a public key, or creating a project stay behind a memorable command instead of a private shell history entry.

## What can it do today?

| Capability | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Git identity | `initx user foo foo@example.com` via `@initx-plugin/git` |
| Copy public keys | `initx cp ssh` or `initx cp gpg` via `@initx-plugin/cp` |
| Project management | `initx pm add ~/projects` and `initx create user/repo` via `@initx-plugin/pm` |
| Plugin extension | Start from `initx-plugin-starter` and publish a package matching the plugin convention |

## Identity and runtime facts

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical CLI package | `initx` |
| Command aliases | `initx`, `ix` |
| Repository | [initx-collective/initx](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx) |
| License | MIT |
| Workspace packages | `initx`, `@initx-plugin/core`, `@initx-plugin/utils` |
| Extension unit | A separately installable `initx-plugin-*` or `@initx-plugin/*` package |

The CLI is the stable host. A plugin owns the user-facing command and its side effects; core and utils provide the shared contract. This means an installed plugin can evolve without turning every workflow into a change to the host CLI.

## Typical scenarios

- A developer wants one command for a setup action used across machines.
- A team wants a small operational workflow to be installed and versioned like a package.
- A plugin author wants to expose a focused capability without implementing argument parsing and host integration from scratch.

Use a project-local task runner when the workflow is tied to one repository's build graph. Use initx when the workflow is a reusable command that should be available independently of a particular checkout.

## Install and learn

- [Getting started](/projects/initx/getting-started) — install the CLI and run the first plugin command.
- [Architecture](/projects/initx/architecture) — understand the CLI, core, utils, and plugin boundary.
- [Reference](/projects/initx/reference) — commands, package names, and runtime terms.
- [Plugin authoring](/projects/initx/plugin-authoring) — create a compatible plugin package.
- [Design decisions](/projects/initx/design-decisions) — why the host/plugin boundary exists.
- [Troubleshooting](/projects/initx/troubleshooting) — resolve install, PATH, and plugin issues.
- [FAQ](/projects/initx/faq) — choose plugins, aliases, and extension paths.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx) — package source, tests, and release history.

## Scope boundary

initx is a local command runner and plugin host. It does not prescribe one deployment platform or replace a full task runner; the plugin is the unit of capability and distribution.

# initx architecture — CLI, core, utils, and plugins

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/architecture/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: initx separates command dispatch from reusable core and utility packages, while plugins provide user-facing scripting capabilities.

# initx architecture

initx is a small monorepo with a clear extension seam: the CLI parses and dispatches commands, core provides shared runtime behavior, utils provides reusable helpers, and plugins turn that foundation into commands users can install.

## Runtime path

```text
shell
  │
  ├─ initx / ix entrypoint
  │    └─ CLI parser and command dispatch
  │         └─ plugin package
  │              └─ task-specific side effects
  │
  └─ shared @initx-plugin/core + @initx-plugin/utils
```

The CLI package publishes the `initx` and `ix` binaries. Its runtime dependencies include `cac` for argument parsing and the workspace core and utils packages for shared behavior.

## Package roles

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `initx` | Published CLI package and binary entrypoint. |
| `@initx-plugin/core` | Shared plugin runtime and command integration. |
| `@initx-plugin/utils` | Shared helpers used by plugins and the CLI. |
| `@initx-plugin/*` | Optional capabilities installed on demand. |

## Extension contract

A plugin should keep its package name in the `initx-plugin-<name>` or `@initx-plugin/<name>` family. The repository's plugin skill recommends using `@initx-plugin/core` and `@initx-plugin/utils` as peer dependencies so plugins share the host runtime instead of bundling competing copies.

## Why the boundary matters

The host can remain stable while capabilities evolve independently. Users install only the workflows they need, and plugin authors can test the task package without changing the command runner itself.

# initx design decisions — why the host is plugin-based

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/design-decisions/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: The design decisions behind initx: a small host CLI, install-on-demand plugins, shared core and utils packages, and the ix alias.

# initx design decisions

## Why make the plugin the unit of capability?

Developer workflows grow at different speeds and have different side effects. Keeping a capability in a plugin means the host can stay small while a user installs only the workflows they recognize and trust.

## Why keep core and utils separate?

The CLI and plugins need shared behavior, but that behavior should have one host contract. `@initx-plugin/core` and `@initx-plugin/utils` provide that contract without forcing every plugin to copy helpers or couple itself to private CLI files.

## Why provide `ix`?

The full `initx` name is useful in documentation and discovery. `ix` is a short alias for repeated terminal use. It is not a second implementation and does not change plugin behavior.

## Why install plugins on demand?

Most users need only a subset of workflows. On-demand installation keeps the default command surface smaller and makes the dependency and permission story visible at the point where a capability is added.

## Why is initx not a full task runner?

Build graphs, project-local pipelines, and dependency scheduling need a different execution model. initx optimizes for portable, user-invoked commands that can be distributed independently of one repository.

## Decision boundary

If a behavior must be shared by every plugin, it belongs in the host packages. If it exists to perform one user workflow, it belongs in the plugin. This boundary is the main architectural invariant.

# initx FAQ — plugins, aliases, and use cases

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/faq/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: Answers to common initx questions about installation, command aliases, plugin naming, and when to use the scripting engine.

# initx FAQ

## Is initx a shell replacement?

No. It is a plugin host for focused, repeatable developer actions. A shell remains the right place for general command composition; initx packages a workflow that deserves a stable name and install path.

## What is the difference between `initx` and `ix`?

They invoke the same CLI entrypoint. `ix` is only the shorter command alias.

## Which plugins are available?

The repository lists Git, GPG, public-key copying, and project-management plugins. The canonical links are in the [project overview](/projects/initx/).

## How do I install a plugin?

Run `initx plugin add <plugin-name>`, for example `initx plugin add git`. The short name maps to the corresponding `@initx-plugin/<name>` package.

## Can I write my own plugin?

Yes. Start with `initx-plugin-starter`, keep the package naming convention, and use the shared core and utils packages as the host contract.

## When should I use a full task runner instead?

Use a full task runner for build graphs, dependency scheduling, or project-local automation. Use initx when the main value is a portable, user-invoked command that can be installed separately.

# initx getting started — install, add plugins, run commands

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/getting-started/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: Install initx globally, use the initx or ix alias, add a plugin, and run a first workflow command.

# Get started with initx

The shortest path is: install the CLI, add a plugin, then run the plugin command. A global install removes the need to prefix every call with `npx`.

## 1. Install the CLI

```bash
npm i -g initx
```

You can use either command name:

```bash
initx <command> [options]
ix <command> [options]
```

## 2. Add a plugin

```bash
initx plugin add git
```

The short name resolves to the published `@initx-plugin/git` package. The same form works for the other official plugins:

```bash
initx plugin add gpg
initx plugin add cp
initx plugin add pm
```

## 3. Run a real workflow

Set a global Git identity:

```bash
initx user foo foo@example.com
```

Copy a public key without opening the key file:

```bash
initx cp ssh
initx cp gpg
```

Register a projects directory once, then create a repository checkout through the project manager plugin:

```bash
initx pm add ~/projects
initx create user/repo
```

## 4. Build a plugin

Use [initx-plugin-starter](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx-plugin-starter) as the starting point. Plugin names follow `initx-plugin-<name>` or `@initx-plugin/<name>` so the CLI and users can recognize them consistently.

## Verify the installation

```bash
initx --help
ix --help
```

If the command is not found, check that the npm global bin directory is on `PATH` and rerun the installation in the same Node.js environment that owns your shell.

# initx plugin authoring — package contract and development path

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/plugin-authoring/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: How to create an initx plugin with the required package naming, shared dependencies, command entrypoint, and local verification flow.

# Author an initx plugin

An initx plugin is a separately installable package that adds a focused command to the host. Start from [initx-plugin-starter](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx-plugin-starter) when possible; it preserves the package shape expected by the ecosystem.

## Package contract

Use one of these names:

```text
initx-plugin-<name>
@initx-plugin/<name>
```

The plugin package should describe the workflow it adds and should expose the host integration through the shared core and utils packages. The repository skill recommends `@initx-plugin/core` and `@initx-plugin/utils` as peer dependencies so a plugin does not bundle a competing host runtime.

## Development path

1. Choose a command name that describes one focused workflow.
2. Create the package from the starter template.
3. Implement the command and keep side effects inside the plugin boundary.
4. Add tests for parsing, success output, and the failure path.
5. Run the plugin through the local initx CLI before publishing.

The initx monorepo uses workspace packages for local development. A plugin maintained elsewhere should consume the published host packages rather than reaching into private source files.

## What belongs in a plugin?

- Task-specific arguments and options.
- User-facing output and actionable errors.
- The external side effect that the command exists to perform.
- Tests that do not require the full initx monorepo when the host contract can be mocked.

## What belongs in the host?

Argument parsing conventions, plugin discovery, shared runtime behavior, and reusable utilities belong in the host packages. Keeping those concerns separate lets users install only the capabilities they need.

## Local verification

From the initx checkout, the repository exposes a local CLI script:

```bash
pnpm ix <command>
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

Use the same command shape after packaging to verify that the published plugin behaves like the workspace version.

# initx reference — commands, packages, and naming

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/reference/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: A factual initx reference for command aliases, plugin package names, workspace packages, and the command grammar users can rely on.

# initx reference

This page is the compact reference for the published initx command surface. Plugin commands are owned by their plugin; the host reference covers the stable installation and dispatch contract.

## Command grammar

```text
initx <command> [options]
ix <command> [options]
```

The two binaries point to the same CLI entrypoint. Use `--help` at the host or plugin level to inspect the installed command surface:

```bash
initx --help
initx plugin --help
ix --help
```

## Host commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `initx plugin add <name>` | Install a plugin by its short or package name. |
| `initx --help` | Show the host CLI help. |
| `ix ...` | Invoke the same host with the short alias. |

The user-facing workflow commands come from plugins. For example, `initx user ...` belongs to the Git plugin, while `initx cp ...` belongs to the public-key copy plugin.

## Package naming

Accepted plugin families are:

```text
initx-plugin-<name>
@initx-plugin/<name>
```

The short form in `initx plugin add git` maps to the corresponding scoped plugin package. Keeping the name convention consistent makes discovery and documentation unambiguous.

## Workspace package roles

| Package | Stable meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `initx` | Published CLI and `initx`/`ix` binaries. |
| `@initx-plugin/core` | Host-facing runtime contract for plugins. |
| `@initx-plugin/utils` | Shared helpers for the CLI and plugins. |

Plugin authors should prefer the shared packages as peer dependencies where the plugin skill requires them. This keeps the host contract singular.

## Source of truth

The [initx repository](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx) is the source for implementation, tests, package versions, and plugin links. This page is an orientation layer; plugin-specific flags belong to the plugin's own documentation.

# initx troubleshooting — PATH, plugins, and local development

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/initx/troubleshooting/
Language: en
Project: initx
Description: Resolve common initx failures involving global installation, PATH, plugin discovery, workspace packages, and local verification.

# initx troubleshooting

## `initx` or `ix` is not found

Check that the npm global bin directory belongs to the same Node.js installation that ran `npm i -g initx`, then open a new shell and run:

```bash
node --version
npm prefix -g
initx --help
```

If `npx initx --help` works but the global command does not, the problem is the shell `PATH`, not the package itself.

## A plugin cannot be found

Use the short name or the full published package name:

```bash
initx plugin add git
initx plugin add @initx-plugin/git
```

Check the package spelling and the registry configured for the current npm environment. Plugin names must follow the initx naming convention.

## A command exists but its options are unknown

The host owns plugin installation, but the plugin owns its workflow flags. Run the plugin command with `--help` and check that the installed plugin version matches the documentation you are reading.

## A workspace plugin behaves differently after publishing

Check whether the plugin is resolving workspace copies of `@initx-plugin/core` or `@initx-plugin/utils`. Test once with the published versions, then compare the package lockfile and peer dependency range.

## Local development fails before the command runs

From the initx checkout, use the repository's own scripts:

```bash
pnpm i
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm ix --help
```

This separates a repository setup problem from a published CLI or plugin problem.

# initx — 插件化脚本引擎

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: initx 是一个 Node.js CLI，通过可安装插件把重复的开发者操作变成 initx 或 ix 命令。

# initx

<p class="lead"><code>initx</code> 是一个面向开发者工作流的插件化脚本引擎。安装 CLI、添加插件，就能把多步 shell 操作变成短命令，同时支持更短的 <code>ix</code> 别名。</p>

维护者：[imba97](/zh/about)。

## 它解决什么问题？

initx 让小型运维脚本有稳定的名字、安装方式和复用边界。CLI 负责分发与插件安装，插件负责具体任务，因此设置 Git、复制公钥、管理项目等操作可以独立演进。

## 当前能力

| 能力 | 示例 |
| --- | --- |
| Git 身份 | 通过 `@initx-plugin/git` 执行 `initx user foo foo@example.com` |
| 复制公钥 | `initx cp ssh` 或 `initx cp gpg` |
| 项目管理 | `initx pm add ~/projects`、`initx create user/repo` |
| 扩展插件 | 使用 `initx-plugin-starter` 创建符合命名约定的插件 |

## 身份与运行事实

| 事实 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| CLI 包 | `initx` |
| 命令别名 | `initx`、`ix` |
| 仓库 | [initx-collective/initx](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx) |
| 许可证 | MIT |
| workspace 包 | `initx`、`@initx-plugin/core`、`@initx-plugin/utils` |
| 扩展单元 | 独立安装的 `initx-plugin-*` 或 `@initx-plugin/*` 包 |

CLI 是稳定宿主；插件负责面向用户的命令和副作用，core 与 utils 提供共享契约。这样插件可以独立演进，不需要每次都修改宿主 CLI。

## 典型场景

- 开发者希望把跨机器重复使用的设置操作变成一个命令。
- 团队希望把小型运维工作流像包一样安装和版本化。
- 插件作者希望复用参数解析和宿主集成，而不是从零实现一套 CLI。

如果流程只服务于一个仓库的构建图，应使用项目内任务运行器；如果流程需要脱离具体 checkout 独立安装，适合使用 initx。

## 边界

initx 是本地命令运行器和插件宿主，不是完整任务编排系统。能力以插件为分发单位。

# initx 架构 — CLI、core、utils 与插件

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/architecture/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: initx 将命令分发与共享运行时拆开，插件提供面向用户的脚本能力。

# initx 架构

initx 是一个小型 monorepo：CLI 解析并分发命令，core 提供共享运行时，utils 提供通用工具，插件把这些能力变成可安装命令。

## 运行路径

```text
shell → initx / ix 入口 → CLI 分发 → 插件包 → 具体副作用
                       ↘ @initx-plugin/core + @initx-plugin/utils
```

## 包的职责

| 包 | 职责 |
| --- | --- |
| `initx` | 发布 CLI 与 `initx`、`ix` 二进制入口。 |
| `@initx-plugin/core` | 共享插件运行时与命令集成。 |
| `@initx-plugin/utils` | CLI 与插件共用的工具。 |
| `@initx-plugin/*` | 按需安装的具体能力。 |

## 扩展约定

插件名保持 `initx-plugin-<name>` 或 `@initx-plugin/<name>`。共享包建议作为 peer dependency，避免每个插件打包一份不同的宿主运行时。

## 这个边界的价值

宿主可以保持稳定，能力则按插件独立发布。用户只安装需要的工作流，插件作者也可以独立测试任务包。

# initx 设计决策 — 为什么采用插件宿主

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/design-decisions/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: 解释 initx 的小型宿主 CLI、按需插件、共享 core/utils 和 ix 别名设计。

# initx 设计决策

## 为什么以插件作为能力单元？

不同开发者工作流的演进速度和副作用不同。把能力放进插件，可以让宿主保持小巧，用户只安装自己需要并且理解的工作流。

## 为什么拆出 core 和 utils？

CLI 与插件需要共享行为，但共享行为应该只有一个宿主契约。`@initx-plugin/core` 与 `@initx-plugin/utils` 提供这个契约，插件不必复制工具或依赖私有 CLI 文件。

## 为什么提供 `ix`？

完整的 `initx` 适合文档和发现；`ix` 适合终端中反复输入。它只是别名，不是第二套实现。

## 为什么按需安装插件？

多数用户只需要部分工作流。按需安装可以缩小默认命令面，也能让能力的依赖和权限在安装时变得清晰。

## 为什么不是完整任务运行器？

构建图、项目内 pipeline 和依赖调度需要另一套执行模型。initx 优先解决可以脱离单个仓库独立安装的用户命令。

## 决策边界

所有插件都需要的行为属于宿主包；只为一个用户工作流存在的行为属于插件。这是主要架构不变量。

# initx FAQ — 插件、别名与使用场景

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/faq/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: 回答 initx 的安装、命令别名、插件命名、扩展方式和适用场景问题。

# initx FAQ

## initx 是 shell 替代品吗？

不是。它是面向小型、可复用开发者操作的插件宿主。通用命令组合仍然适合放在 shell 中。

## `initx` 和 `ix` 有什么区别？

它们调用同一个 CLI，`ix` 只是更短的命令别名。

## 如何安装插件？

运行 `initx plugin add <plugin-name>`，例如 `initx plugin add git`。

## 可以写自己的插件吗？

可以。从 `initx-plugin-starter` 开始，遵循命名约定，并复用共享 core 与 utils。

## 什么时候应该用完整任务运行器？

如果需要构建依赖图、调度或项目内自动化，使用完整任务运行器；如果需要一个可独立安装、可记忆的工作流命令，使用 initx。

# initx 快速开始 — 安装、添加插件、运行命令

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/getting-started/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: 全局安装 initx，使用 initx 或 ix 别名，添加插件并运行第一个工作流命令。

# initx 快速开始

最短路径是：安装 CLI、添加插件、运行插件命令。全局安装后不需要每次都写 `npx`。

## 1. 安装 CLI

```bash
npm i -g initx
```

```bash
initx <command> [options]
ix <command> [options]
```

## 2. 添加插件

```bash
initx plugin add git
initx plugin add gpg
initx plugin add cp
initx plugin add pm
```

短名称会映射到对应的 `@initx-plugin/<name>` 包。

## 3. 运行工作流

```bash
initx user foo foo@example.com
initx cp ssh
initx cp gpg
initx pm add ~/projects
initx create user/repo
```

## 4. 创建插件

从 [initx-plugin-starter](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx-plugin-starter) 开始。插件名遵循 `initx-plugin-<name>` 或 `@initx-plugin/<name>`，并建议复用 `@initx-plugin/core` 与 `@initx-plugin/utils`。

## 验证

```bash
initx --help
ix --help
```

# initx 插件开发 — 包契约与开发路径

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/plugin-authoring/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: 介绍 initx 插件的包命名、共享依赖、命令入口、本地验证和发布前检查。

# initx 插件开发

initx 插件是一个独立安装的包，为宿主增加一个聚焦的命令。优先从 [initx-plugin-starter](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx-plugin-starter) 开始。

## 包契约

使用以下名称之一：

```text
initx-plugin-<name>
@initx-plugin/<name>
```

插件应描述自己增加的工作流，并通过共享 core 与 utils 接入宿主。项目 skill 建议把 `@initx-plugin/core` 与 `@initx-plugin/utils` 作为 peer dependency，避免插件打包另一份宿主运行时。

## 开发路径

1. 选择一个描述单一工作流的命令名。
2. 从 starter 模板创建包。
3. 实现命令，把副作用留在插件边界内。
4. 为解析、成功输出和失败路径增加测试。
5. 在发布前通过本地 initx CLI 运行插件。

initx monorepo 用 workspace 包做本地开发；独立维护的插件应依赖已发布的宿主包，不要依赖私有源码路径。

## 插件应该包含什么？

- 工作流专属的参数和选项。
- 面向用户的输出与可执行错误信息。
- 这个命令存在的具体外部副作用。
- 可以独立运行的解析和行为测试。

宿主负责插件发现、共享运行时和通用工具；插件负责具体能力。

## 本地验证

在 initx checkout 中可以使用：

```bash
pnpm ix <command>
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

打包后再用同一组命令验证发布插件与 workspace 版本的行为一致。

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/reference/

# initx 参考手册

这是 initx 已发布命令面的简明参考。插件命令由插件自己负责，宿主参考只描述稳定的安装与分发契约。

## 命令语法

```bash
initx <command> [options]
ix <command> [options]
```

两个二进制指向同一个 CLI 入口：

```bash
initx --help
initx plugin --help
ix --help
```

## 宿主命令

| 命令 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `initx plugin add <name>` | 按短名称或包名安装插件。 |
| `initx --help` | 查看宿主 CLI 帮助。 |
| `ix ...` | 使用短别名调用同一个宿主。 |

具体工作流命令来自插件。例如 `initx user ...` 属于 Git 插件，`initx cp ...` 属于公钥复制插件。

## 包命名

插件使用以下命名族：

```text
initx-plugin-<name>
@initx-plugin/<name>
```

`initx plugin add git` 这样的短名称会映射到对应的 scoped 包。保持命名约定可以避免安装和文档歧义。

## workspace 包职责

| 包 | 稳定含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `initx` | 发布 CLI 与 `initx`/`ix` 二进制。 |
| `@initx-plugin/core` | 面向插件的宿主运行时契约。 |
| `@initx-plugin/utils` | CLI 与插件共用的工具。 |

插件应按项目约定优先把共享包作为 peer dependency，保持宿主契约唯一。

## 事实来源

[initx 仓库](https://github.com/initx-collective/initx) 是实现、测试、版本和插件链接的来源。本页只做导航，插件自己的 flags 应以插件文档为准。

# initx 故障排查 — PATH、插件与本地开发

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/initx/troubleshooting/
Language: zh-CN
Project: initx
Description: 解决 initx 全局安装、PATH、插件发现、workspace 包和本地验证问题。

# initx 故障排查

## 找不到 `initx` 或 `ix`

确认 npm 全局 bin 目录属于执行 `npm i -g initx` 的同一个 Node.js 环境，然后重新打开终端：

```bash
node --version
npm prefix -g
initx --help
```

如果 `npx initx --help` 可以运行而全局命令不行，通常是 shell 的 `PATH` 问题。

## 找不到插件

可以使用短名称或完整包名：

```bash
initx plugin add git
initx plugin add @initx-plugin/git
```

检查包名、registry 和当前 npm 环境。插件名必须符合 initx 命名约定。

## 命令存在但选项不认识

宿主负责安装，插件负责工作流 flags。对具体插件执行 `--help`，并确认插件版本与文档版本一致。

## workspace 插件和发布版本行为不同

确认插件是否解析到了 workspace 里的 `@initx-plugin/core` 或 `@initx-plugin/utils`。用已发布版本再测试一次，并比较 lockfile 与 peer dependency 范围。

## 本地开发在命令执行前失败

在 initx 仓库中使用项目自己的脚本：

```bash
pnpm i
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm ix --help
```

这样可以区分仓库环境问题和已发布 CLI/插件问题。

## Project: Mail Peon

# Mail Peon — local-first AI mail assistant

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Mail Peon is a Chrome and Firefox Manifest V3 extension that surfaces important mail and auto-copies verification codes.

# Mail Peon

<p class="lead"><strong>Mail Peon</strong> is a local-first AI mail assistant for Chrome and Firefox. It watches the mail you choose, extracts verification codes, summarizes important messages, and keeps the working data in the extension's local IndexedDB.</p>

Maintainer: [imba97](/about).

## What problem does Mail Peon solve?

Mail Peon reduces the time between “a message arrived” and “I know what needs action.” Its minimal mode focuses on verification and confirmation mail; its custom mode adds a mail stream, AI summaries, prompt rules, exclusions, and badge status.

## Core capabilities

| Capability | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Verification codes | Extracts a code, copies it through a fallback chain, and shows a page-top toast with expiry timing when available. |
| Local-first storage | Accounts, rules, and mail records live in IndexedDB owned by the extension. Minimal mode does not retain the message body. |
| Mail providers | Gmail uses OAuth; IMAP uses a local WebSocket-to-TCP relay because MV3 cannot open raw TCP. |
| AI providers | OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, with validated output and custom prompt rules. |
| Sync model | First connection records a cursor; later syncs fetch incrementally in batches of at most 50 messages. |

## Modes and operating facts

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Product name | Mail Peon |
| Package and repository name | `mail-peon` |
| Runtime | Chrome and Firefox Manifest V3 extension |
| Local database | Extension-owned IndexedDB database named `mail-peon` |
| Mail providers | Gmail OAuth and IMAP through a local relay |
| Default polling interval | 5 minutes, configurable from 1 to 60 minutes |

**Minimal mode** is a narrow path for verification and confirmation mail. It extracts the code, gives a toast, and drops unrelated messages instead of storing them. **Custom mode** is the mail-stream path: it keeps configurable message types, AI summaries, prompt rules, exclusions, ad filtering, and badge status.

## Typical scenarios

- A developer is registering for services and wants a code copied without switching to a mailbox tab.
- A user monitors several accounts and wants only actionable mail surfaced in the browser.
- A privacy-conscious user wants message state in local browser storage while choosing which provider receives AI input.

Mail Peon remains an assistant around an existing mailbox. It does not send mail, replace provider search, or provide a hosted team inbox.

## Install and learn

- [Getting started](/projects/mail-peon/getting-started) — build the extension and connect Gmail or IMAP.
- [Architecture](/projects/mail-peon/architecture) — see the MV3 service worker, relay, UI, and storage boundaries.
- [Reference](/projects/mail-peon/reference) — modes, settings, providers, and message lifecycle terms.
- [Privacy and security](/projects/mail-peon/privacy) — local data, AI input, credentials, and relay trust.
- [Providers and sync](/projects/mail-peon/providers-and-sync) — Gmail, IMAP, cursors, and incremental fetch behavior.
- [Troubleshooting](/projects/mail-peon/troubleshooting) — resolve relay, AI, permissions, and sync failures.
- [FAQ](/projects/mail-peon/faq) — understand privacy, modes, and provider requirements.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/mail-peon/mail-peon) — implementation, design docs, and release checks.

## Scope boundary

Mail Peon is an assistant around an existing mailbox. It does not replace Gmail or another mail UI, send mail, or store your mailbox in a hosted service.

# Mail Peon architecture — MV3, relay, AI, and IndexedDB

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/architecture/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Mail Peon separates the MV3 background service worker, browser UI, local relay, content script, AI providers, and IndexedDB storage.

# Mail Peon architecture

Mail Peon keeps privileged work in the background service worker and keeps UI contexts focused on rendering and messaging. A local relay exists only for IMAP transport; it does not become a hosted mail service.

## Runtime topology

```text
Gmail OAuth ───────────────┐
IMAP server ← TLS ← relay ←┼─ WebSocket ─ Background service worker
                            │                         │
                     Popup / Options / Sidepanel ←──┤
                                                     ├─ IndexedDB
                                                     ├─ AI provider
                                                     └─ Content-script toast + clipboard fallback
```

## Responsibility by context

| Context | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Background service worker | Connects providers, parses mail, calls AI, writes IndexedDB, updates badge, and sends toast events. |
| Local IMAP relay | Holds the long-lived IMAP `IDLE` connection and moves bytes between WebSocket and TCP. It does not parse message content. |
| Popup | Shows the recent important mail list. |
| Sidepanel | Shows the expanded mail stream and filters. |
| Options | Edits accounts, AI providers, prompt rules, exclusions, and general settings. |
| Content script | Renders an isolated top-page toast and retries clipboard writes in the page focus context. |

## Data and privacy boundary

Accounts, rules, and messages are stored in the extension's IndexedDB. Minimal mode does not store message bodies. When AI is enabled, the configured provider receives only the text needed for its task. IMAP credentials are stored locally, and the relay can see decrypted IMAP bytes because it terminates the TLS connection; keep it bound to localhost and protect any token.

## Sync semantics

The first connection records a cursor instead of downloading history. Later runs fetch incrementally, with each batch capped at 50 messages. A changed IMAP `UIDVALIDITY` resets the cursor to the newest position and warns the user instead of guessing how to recover old state.

# Mail Peon FAQ — modes, privacy, Gmail, and IMAP

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/faq/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Answers to common Mail Peon questions about browser support, mailbox providers, local storage, AI, and the IMAP relay.

# Mail Peon FAQ

## Is Mail Peon a replacement for Gmail?

No. It is a browser-side assistant around an existing mailbox. It surfaces important messages and helps with codes and summaries; writing and full mailbox search remain in the mail provider's UI.

## What is the difference between Minimal and Custom mode?

Minimal mode is for verification and confirmation mail and discards unrelated mail. Custom mode keeps a configurable mail stream and adds AI summaries, prompt rules, ad filtering, exclusions, and badge status.

## Does it support Gmail and IMAP?

Yes. Gmail uses OAuth directly. IMAP requires the included local WebSocket-to-TCP relay because a browser MV3 service worker cannot open a raw TCP socket.

## Where is mail stored?

In the extension's own IndexedDB. Minimal mode intentionally does not keep the message body. There is no hosted Mail Peon mailbox.

## Is an AI key required?

Yes for AI extraction and summaries. Configure a supported provider in the options page. Custom mode can fall back to basic message information when an AI call fails; Minimal mode drops a message if it cannot extract the needed code.

## Why does the relay see plaintext?

The relay terminates IMAP TLS so it can maintain a TCP connection and speak IMAP on behalf of the browser. Run it locally, use a token when needed, and do not expose it to the public internet.

# Mail Peon getting started — build, connect, and configure

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/getting-started/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Build the Mail Peon browser extension, connect Gmail with OAuth or IMAP through a local relay, then configure an AI provider.

# Get started with Mail Peon

Mail Peon is loaded as an unpacked browser extension during development. The first setup has three parts: build the extension, connect a mailbox, and configure an AI key.

## 1. Build the extension

```bash
pnpm i
pnpm build
```

Then open the browser extension page (`chrome://extensions` in Chrome), enable developer mode, and load the generated `extension/` directory.

For development with hot rebuilds:

```bash
pnpm dev
```

## 2. Connect a mailbox

### Gmail

Create a Google Cloud OAuth client for a Chrome extension, then enter the client details in **Settings → Accounts**. Gmail uses OAuth and does not require the relay.

### IMAP

Run the included relay locally:

```bash
pnpm relay
pnpm relay --port 9000 --token xxx --allow-hosts imap.example.com
```

Use `ws://127.0.0.1:41316/` in the extension, then enter the IMAP host, username, and password. The relay is required because browser MV3 contexts expose `fetch` and WebSocket, not raw TCP.

## 3. Configure AI

Open **Settings → AI configuration**, select OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, enter an API key, and use **Test connection**. Minimal mode also needs AI because it uses a short extraction prompt for verification codes.

## 4. Pick a mode

- **Minimal mode** keeps only the information needed for verification and confirmation mail. Other mail is discarded instead of being stored or displayed.
- **Custom mode** adds the mail stream, AI summaries, ad filtering, prompt rules, exclusions, and badge updates.

The interval checker defaults to five minutes. Opening the popup also triggers an immediate check, and **Sync now** starts an incremental sync manually.

# Mail Peon privacy and security — local data, AI input, and relay trust

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/privacy/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: How Mail Peon stores credentials and mail locally, what an AI provider receives, and why the IMAP relay is a local trust boundary.

# Mail Peon privacy and security

Mail Peon is local-first, but local-first does not mean no data leaves the browser. The relevant question is which data is stored locally, which data is sent to the configured AI provider, and which process can see IMAP plaintext.

## Storage classification

| Data | Location | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IMAP password, OAuth token, AI key | Extension IndexedDB | Stored locally by the extension; treat the browser profile as a credential store. |
| Accounts and prompt rules | Extension IndexedDB | Used by the background worker and options UI. |
| Message records | Extension IndexedDB in Custom mode | Retention and trash behavior are local settings and code paths. |
| Message body | Not retained in Minimal mode | Minimal mode keeps only the information needed for its narrow workflow. |
| AI input | Configured AI provider | Only sent when an AI operation is enabled and invoked. |

## AI boundary

The user chooses the provider and supplies its key. AI output is validated before the extension uses it. Custom mode can fall back to basic message information when AI fails; Minimal mode does not retain a message when it cannot extract the code it needs.

## IMAP relay boundary

The browser cannot open raw TCP from an MV3 service worker, so IMAP uses a local WebSocket-to-TCP relay. The relay terminates the mail server's TLS connection and can therefore see decrypted bytes, including credentials. Keep it bound to `127.0.0.1`, protect the optional token, and do not expose it publicly.

## Browser permissions and user controls

The extension's background context owns network and storage work. The options UI exposes provider, account, rule, retention, and mode controls. Users should remove credentials from the extension before sharing a browser profile or an exported development environment.

## Threat model

Mail Peon reduces hosted data collection; it does not protect a compromised browser profile, a malicious local process, or an AI provider that receives content by explicit configuration. The most important control is choosing the provider and keeping the relay local.

# Mail Peon providers and sync — Gmail, IMAP, cursors, and batches

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/providers-and-sync/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Compare Mail Peon Gmail and IMAP connection paths and understand first sync, cursors, batching, and UIDVALIDITY behavior.

# Mail Peon providers and sync

## Provider comparison

| Provider | Authentication | Transport | Extra process |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gmail | Google OAuth client and token | Gmail REST API | None |
| IMAP | Host, port, TLS, username, password | IMAP over a local WebSocket-to-TCP relay | Relay required |

Gmail is the shorter setup path. IMAP supports a broader set of mail servers but needs the relay because browser MV3 contexts do not expose raw TCP sockets.

## First connection

The first connection records the current cursor instead of downloading a mailbox history. This prevents a new installation from flooding the local store with old messages and gives the user a predictable starting point.

## Incremental sync

Later checks fetch only messages after the provider cursor. Each batch is capped at 50 messages. The background worker parses and classifies messages before writing local records and updating UI signals.

## Polling and manual sync

The general setting defaults to a five-minute check and accepts an interval from one to 60 minutes. Opening the popup checks immediately, and the options page can trigger an incremental sync manually.

## IMAP UIDVALIDITY changes

IMAP uses `UIDVALIDITY` to identify the meaning of message UIDs in a mailbox. If it changes, Mail Peon resets the cursor to the newest position and warns the user rather than pretending that the old cursor is still valid.

## What the relay does not do

The relay holds a long-lived IMAP `IDLE` connection and moves bytes between WebSocket and TCP. It does not own the UI, classify messages, call AI, or persist a hosted mailbox.

# Mail Peon reference — modes, settings, and message lifecycle

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/reference/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: A factual Mail Peon reference for modes, accounts, AI providers, prompt rules, message states, and browser UI contexts.

# Mail Peon reference

## Product and package names

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Mail Peon | Product name shown in the extension UI and manifest. |
| `mail-peon` | Repository, package, IndexedDB, log, and message-channel name. |

Keeping those names separate avoids confusing a user-facing label with an implementation identifier.

## Modes

| Mode | Stored message behavior | Main output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal | Unrelated messages are discarded; message bodies are not retained. | Verification code, confirmation action, page-top toast. |
| Custom | Configurable mail records and summaries are kept locally. | Mail stream, AI summary, badge, filters, and prompt rules. |

The mode switch does not require a separate account or a new installation, and switching modes does not clear the existing local data.

## Account fields

An account identifies a provider and its connection state. Gmail uses OAuth client data and a token. IMAP uses host, port, TLS, username, password, relay URL, and an incremental cursor.

## Prompt rules

A prompt rule matches a sender address, domain, or regular expression and supplies a provider-specific instruction. Rules have priority ordering; smaller priority values run first. Exclusion entries can prevent a sender from entering the extension at all.

## Message lifecycle

```text
provider → fetch → parse → classify → AI extraction/summary → local store → UI/toast
```

Minimal mode may stop after extraction and toast delivery. Custom mode can retain the local message record, move deleted messages to a recoverable trash state, and later remove them permanently.

## UI contexts

| Context | Primary job |
| --- | --- |
| Popup | Recent important messages. |
| Sidepanel | Expanded mail stream and filters. |
| Options | Accounts, AI, rules, exclusions, and general settings. |
| Content script | Isolated toast rendering and clipboard fallback. |

# Mail Peon troubleshooting — extension, relay, AI, and sync failures

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/mail-peon/troubleshooting/
Language: en
Project: mail-peon
Description: Resolve common Mail Peon failures involving unpacked extension loading, OAuth, the IMAP relay, AI providers, clipboard, and incremental sync.

# Mail Peon troubleshooting

## The extension does not appear

Run `pnpm build`, open the browser extension management page, enable developer mode, and load the generated `extension/` directory. If an old build is still loaded, remove it before loading the new directory.

## Gmail authentication does not finish

Confirm that the OAuth client is created for a Chrome extension and that the client ID in the extension matches the one in the Google Cloud project. Check the background service worker console for the provider error before changing account settings.

## IMAP connection fails immediately

Start the relay and verify the exact WebSocket URL:

```bash
pnpm relay
```

The default is `ws://127.0.0.1:41316/`. If a custom port or token is used, copy the same values into the account settings. Keep the relay bound to localhost while diagnosing it.

## The relay starts but no mail arrives

Check the IMAP host, port, TLS mode, username, and mailbox selection. Confirm that the relay can reach the server and that the extension's background worker is still active. A first connection records a cursor and intentionally does not download history.

## AI summaries or code extraction fail

Test the selected provider from **Settings → AI configuration**. Verify the API key, endpoint, model, and provider compatibility. Custom mode can show basic message data after an AI failure; Minimal mode drops a message if the code cannot be extracted.

## The code was found but not copied

The copy path falls back from the background context to the content-script toast and then to a user-click action. Focus a normal web page, allow clipboard access, and use the toast's copy button if the automatic attempt was blocked.

## A message seems to be missing

Check the mode, exclusion list, sender prompt rules, and the selected account. In Minimal mode, unrelated mail is intentionally discarded. In Custom mode, inspect the background logs and the local trash state before assuming permanent deletion.

# Mail Peon — 本地优先的 AI 邮件助手

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: Mail Peon 是一个支持 Chrome 与 Firefox 的 Manifest V3 扩展，用于找出重要邮件并自动复制验证码。

# Mail Peon

<p class="lead"><strong>Mail Peon</strong> 是一个本地优先的 AI 邮件助手，支持 Chrome 与 Firefox。它提取验证码、摘要重要邮件，并把工作数据存放在扩展自己的 IndexedDB 中。</p>

维护者：[imba97](/zh/about)。

## 它解决什么问题？

Mail Peon 缩短“邮件到达”与“知道该做什么”之间的时间。极简模式专注验证码和确认邮件；自定义模式增加邮件流、AI 摘要、提示词规则、排除列表和 badge。

## 核心能力

| 能力 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| 验证码 | 提取并复制验证码；有有效期时显示倒计时信息。 |
| 本地优先 | 账号、规则和邮件存于扩展 IndexedDB；极简模式不保存正文。 |
| 邮箱协议 | Gmail 使用 OAuth；IMAP 通过本机 WebSocket-TCP 中继。 |
| AI 平台 | 支持 OpenAI、DeepSeek、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 兼容服务。 |
| 增量同步 | 首次只记录游标，之后按批次拉取，每批最多 50 封。 |

## 模式与运行事实

| 事实 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| 产品名 | Mail Peon |
| 包名与仓库名 | `mail-peon` |
| 运行环境 | Chrome 与 Firefox Manifest V3 扩展 |
| 本地数据库 | 扩展自己的 IndexedDB，数据库名为 `mail-peon` |
| 邮箱协议 | Gmail OAuth、经本机中继的 IMAP |
| 默认检查间隔 | 5 分钟，可配置为 1–60 分钟 |

**极简模式**只处理验证码和确认邮件：提取验证码、显示 toast，其他邮件不入库。**自定义模式**提供邮件流、可配置类型、AI 摘要、提示词规则、排除列表、广告过滤和 badge。

## 典型场景

- 注册服务时，希望不用切换邮箱标签页就复制验证码。
- 管理多个账号时，只想看到真正需要处理的邮件。
- 希望邮件状态保存在本地浏览器，同时明确控制哪些内容发送给 AI 提供商。

Mail Peon 仍然是现有邮箱的助手，不负责发信、不替代邮箱搜索，也不提供云端团队收件箱。

# Mail Peon 架构 — MV3、中继、AI 与 IndexedDB

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/architecture/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: Mail Peon 将 MV3 后台、浏览器 UI、本机中继、content script、AI 提供商和 IndexedDB 分开。

# Mail Peon 架构

Mail Peon 将需要权限的工作放在后台 service worker，UI 只负责渲染与通信。本机中继只承担 IMAP 传输，不是云端邮件服务。

## 运行拓扑

```text
Gmail OAuth ───────────────┐
IMAP ← TLS ← 本机中继 ←───┼─ WebSocket ─ 后台 service worker
                           │                         │
                    Popup / Options / Sidepanel ←──┤
                                                     ├─ IndexedDB
                                                     ├─ AI 提供商
                                                     └─ toast + clipboard fallback
```

## 上下文职责

| 上下文 | 职责 |
| --- | --- |
| Background service worker | 连接邮箱、解析邮件、调用 AI、写 IndexedDB、更新 badge、发送 toast。 |
| 本机 IMAP 中继 | 维护 `IDLE` 长连接并搬运 WebSocket/TCP 字节，不解析正文。 |
| Popup | 展示最近的重要邮件。 |
| Sidepanel | 展开展示邮件流和过滤项。 |
| Options | 编辑账号、AI、提示词、排除项和通用设置。 |
| Content script | 用隔离的顶部 toast 反馈，并在页面焦点上下文重试复制。 |

## 数据与隐私边界

账号、规则和邮件存储在扩展 IndexedDB。极简模式不保存正文。启用 AI 时只向用户配置的提供商发送任务所需文本。IMAP 中继因为要终止 TLS 能看到解密字节，应绑定 localhost 并保护 token。

## 同步语义

首次连接只记录游标，不下载历史；之后增量同步，每批最多 50 封。IMAP `UIDVALIDITY` 变化时会重置到最新位置并提醒用户。

# Mail Peon FAQ — 模式、隐私、Gmail 与 IMAP

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/faq/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: 回答 Mail Peon 关于浏览器支持、邮箱协议、本地存储、AI 和 IMAP 中继的常见问题。

# Mail Peon FAQ

## Mail Peon 是 Gmail 的替代品吗？

不是。它围绕现有邮箱提供验证码、摘要和重要邮件提示；写信和完整搜索仍在邮箱 UI 中完成。

## 极简模式和自定义模式有什么区别？

极简模式只处理验证码与确认邮件，其他邮件丢弃。自定义模式保留可配置邮件流，并提供摘要、提示词、广告过滤、排除项和 badge。

## 支持 Gmail 和 IMAP 吗？

支持。Gmail 直接使用 OAuth；IMAP 需要本机 WebSocket-TCP 中继，因为 MV3 service worker 不能打开裸 TCP。

## 邮件存在哪里？

在扩展自己的 IndexedDB 中。极简模式不保存正文，也不存在云端 Mail Peon 邮箱。

## 必须配置 AI Key 吗？

需要进行 AI 提取和摘要。自定义模式的 AI 调用失败时可以退化为基础邮件信息；极简模式无法提取验证码时会丢弃该邮件。

## 为什么中继能看到明文？

中继要终止 IMAP TLS 才能维护 TCP 连接并代表浏览器说 IMAP，因此会看到明文。请只在本机运行，不要暴露到公网。

# Mail Peon 快速开始 — 构建、接入邮箱与配置 AI

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/getting-started/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: 构建 Mail Peon 扩展，通过 OAuth 接入 Gmail 或通过本机中继接入 IMAP，再配置 AI 提供商。

# Mail Peon 快速开始

开发阶段以未打包扩展运行。第一次使用包含三步：构建扩展、接入邮箱、配置 AI Key。

## 1. 构建扩展

```bash
pnpm i
pnpm build
```

在 Chrome 的 `chrome://extensions` 打开开发者模式，加载生成的 `extension/` 目录。开发时可以使用：

```bash
pnpm dev
```

## 2. 接入邮箱

### Gmail

创建类型为 Chrome 扩展的 Google Cloud OAuth 客户端，在“设置 · 账号”中填写。Gmail 不需要中继。

### IMAP

```bash
pnpm relay
pnpm relay --port 9000 --token xxx --allow-hosts imap.example.com
```

在扩展中填写 `ws://127.0.0.1:41316/`，再填写 IMAP 主机、用户名和密码。MV3 没有裸 TCP，所以 IMAP 必须经过中继。

## 3. 配置 AI

进入“设置 · AI 配置”，选择 OpenAI、DeepSeek、Anthropic 或 OpenAI 兼容服务，填写 API Key 并测试连接。极简模式提取验证码同样需要 AI。

## 4. 选择模式

- **极简模式**：只保留验证码和确认邮件相关信息，其它邮件不入库、不展示。
- **自定义模式**：增加邮件流、AI 摘要、广告过滤、提示词规则、排除列表和 badge。

默认每 5 分钟检查一次；打开 Popup 会立即检查，也可以手动执行增量同步。

# Mail Peon 隐私与安全 — 本地数据、AI 输入与中继信任

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/privacy/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: 说明 Mail Peon 如何本地存储凭据和邮件、AI 提供商收到什么，以及 IMAP 中继为什么是本地信任边界。

# Mail Peon 隐私与安全

Mail Peon 是本地优先，但这不等于没有数据离开浏览器。需要区分哪些数据只在本地、哪些数据会发送给 AI 提供商，以及哪个进程能够看到 IMAP 明文。

## 数据分类

| 数据 | 位置 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IMAP 密码、OAuth token、AI key | 扩展 IndexedDB | 存在本地，浏览器 profile 应被视为凭据存储。 |
| 账号与提示词规则 | 扩展 IndexedDB | 由 background 和 options 使用。 |
| 邮件记录 | 自定义模式的扩展 IndexedDB | 受本地保留与回收站逻辑影响。 |
| 邮件正文 | 极简模式不保留 | 极简模式只保留窄工作流所需信息。 |
| AI 输入 | 用户配置的 AI 提供商 | 仅在启用并触发 AI 操作时发送。 |

## AI 边界

用户选择提供商并填写 key，AI 输出会先经过校验。自定义模式调用失败时仍可展示基础邮件信息；极简模式无法提取验证码时不保留该邮件。

## IMAP 中继边界

MV3 service worker 不能打开裸 TCP，所以 IMAP 通过本机 WebSocket-TCP 中继。中继要终止邮件服务器 TLS，因此能看到包括凭据在内的解密字节。应绑定 `127.0.0.1`、保护 token，不要暴露到公网。

## 用户控制

background 负责网络和存储，options 暴露 provider、账号、规则、保留、模式等设置。共享浏览器 profile 或开发环境前，应先移除凭据。

## 威胁模型

Mail Peon 减少云端托管数据，但不能保护被入侵的浏览器 profile、恶意本机进程，或用户明确配置后接收内容的 AI 提供商。最重要的控制是选择提供商并保持中继在本机。

# Mail Peon 邮箱与同步 — Gmail、IMAP、游标与批次

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/providers-and-sync/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: 对比 Mail Peon 的 Gmail 和 IMAP 连接路径，说明首次同步、游标、批量拉取和 UIDVALIDITY 行为。

# Mail Peon 邮箱与同步

## 协议对比

| 提供商 | 认证 | 传输 | 额外进程 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gmail | Google OAuth client 与 token | Gmail REST API | 无 |
| IMAP | host、port、TLS、用户名、密码 | 经本机 WebSocket-TCP 中继的 IMAP | 需要中继 |

Gmail 配置更短；IMAP 覆盖更多邮件服务器，但浏览器 MV3 没有裸 TCP，所以需要中继。

## 首次连接

首次连接只记录当前位置的游标，不下载历史邮件。这样新安装不会把旧邮箱一次性灌入本地存储，也能让起始状态可预测。

## 增量同步

后续检查只拉取游标之后的新邮件，每批最多 50 封。background 会在写入本地记录和更新 UI 信号前解析、分类邮件。

## 轮询与手动同步

通用设置默认每 5 分钟检查一次，可设为 1–60 分钟。打开 Popup 会立即检查，Options 也可以手动触发增量同步。

## IMAP UIDVALIDITY 变化

`UIDVALIDITY` 变化意味着原有 UID 的含义不再可靠。Mail Peon 会重置到最新位置并提醒用户，不会假设旧游标仍然有效。

## 中继不负责什么？

中继只维护 IMAP `IDLE` 长连接并搬运 WebSocket/TCP 字节，不负责 UI、分类、AI 或云端邮箱存储。

# Mail Peon 参考手册 — 模式、设置与邮件生命周期

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/reference/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: Mail Peon 的模式、账号、AI 提供商、提示词规则、邮件状态和浏览器 UI 上下文参考。

# Mail Peon 参考手册

## 产品名与包名

| 名称 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| Mail Peon | 扩展 UI 和 manifest 中的产品名。 |
| `mail-peon` | 仓库、包、IndexedDB、日志和消息通道名称。 |

## 模式

| 模式 | 邮件存储行为 | 主要输出 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 极简 | 无关邮件丢弃，不保存正文。 | 验证码、确认动作、顶部 toast。 |
| 自定义 | 本地保存可配置邮件记录和摘要。 | 邮件流、AI 摘要、badge、过滤器、提示词规则。 |

模式切换不需要重新安装，也不会自动清空已有本地数据。

## 账号字段

账号包含 provider 和连接状态。Gmail 使用 OAuth client 与 token；IMAP 使用 host、port、TLS、用户名、密码、relay URL 和增量游标。

## 提示词规则

规则可以匹配发件人地址、域名或正则，并为该来源提供专属指令。规则按 priority 排序，数值越小越先执行；排除项可以阻止来源进入扩展。

## 邮件生命周期

```text
provider → 拉取 → 解析 → 分类 → AI 提取/摘要 → 本地存储 → UI/toast
```

极简模式可能在提取和 toast 后结束；自定义模式可以保存本地记录、将删除邮件放入可恢复回收站，再按需要彻底删除。

## UI 上下文

| 上下文 | 主要职责 |
| --- | --- |
| Popup | 最近的重要邮件。 |
| Sidepanel | 展开邮件流和过滤。 |
| Options | 账号、AI、规则、排除和通用设置。 |
| Content script | 隔离 toast 和剪贴板 fallback。 |

# Mail Peon 故障排查 — 扩展、中继、AI 与同步

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/mail-peon/troubleshooting/
Language: zh-CN
Project: mail-peon
Description: 解决 Mail Peon 未打包扩展、OAuth、IMAP 中继、AI、剪贴板和增量同步问题。

# Mail Peon 故障排查

## 扩展没有出现

执行 `pnpm build`，打开浏览器扩展管理页，启用开发者模式并加载生成的 `extension/` 目录。旧版本仍在运行时，先移除再加载新目录。

## Gmail OAuth 无法完成

确认 OAuth client 类型是 Chrome 扩展，且扩展中的 client ID 与 Google Cloud 项目一致。先查看 background service worker 控制台中的 provider 错误，再修改账号设置。

## IMAP 一启动就失败

先启动中继并确认 WebSocket 地址：

```bash
pnpm relay
```

默认地址是 `ws://127.0.0.1:41316/`。如果使用了自定义端口或 token，扩展账号设置必须使用相同值。

## 中继运行但没有邮件

检查 IMAP host、port、TLS、用户名和 mailbox。确认中继能连接服务器，且 background 仍在运行。首次连接只记录游标，不下载历史邮件。

## AI 摘要或验证码提取失败

在“设置 · AI 配置”测试选中的 provider，检查 API key、endpoint、model 和兼容性。自定义模式可以退化到基础邮件信息；极简模式提取失败时会丢弃该邮件。

## 找到验证码但没有复制

复制流程会从 background fallback 到 content script toast，最后允许用户点击复制。聚焦普通网页、允许剪贴板权限，并使用 toast 上的复制按钮。

## 邮件似乎丢失

检查模式、排除列表、发件人规则和账号。极简模式会有意丢弃无关邮件；自定义模式应查看 background 日志和本地回收站状态。

---

## Project: cargo-bumpp

# cargo-bumpp — interactive Cargo release versioning

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: cargo-bumpp is a zero-dependency Rust CLI that bumps Cargo versions, updates the lockfile, commits, tags, and pushes.

# cargo-bumpp

<p class="lead"><code>cargo-bumpp</code> is an interactive, zero-dependency release helper for Cargo projects. It selects or receives a release level, updates manifests and <code>Cargo.lock</code>, shows a plan, then commits, tags, and pushes after one confirmation.</p>

Maintainer: [imba97](/about).

## What problem does cargo-bumpp solve?

It makes the common “bump → commit → annotated tag → push” path explicit and reviewable. The tool stops at the tag; a CI workflow remains responsible for publishing to a registry.

## Key behavior

| Behavior | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Install cost | `cargo install cargo-bumpp`; the crate has no runtime dependencies. |
| Version inputs | Interactive selector, `major`, `minor`, `patch`, `conventional`, prerelease levels, or an explicit version. |
| Workspace handling | Uses `cargo metadata` to understand shared versions and path dependencies; `--recursive` opts into independent member bumps. |
| Safety | Shows changed files and line numbers, confirms once, rolls back local changes if steps 3–5 fail, and does not roll back after a push failure. |
| Release boundary | Creates the release point but deliberately does not publish to crates.io or create a PR flow. |

## Release model

The default run has one visible decision and six operational stages:

1. Select a release level or explicit version.
2. Read Cargo metadata and Git history when the mode needs them.
3. Print every version change, including manifest paths and line numbers.
4. Ask for one confirmation, then write manifests and `Cargo.lock`.
5. Create the release commit and annotated tag.
6. Push the branch and the exact tag, unless a `--no-push` option is used.

The local mutation stages are rollback-aware. A failure before push restores the working tree, commit, and tag. A remote push failure leaves the local release point intact and prints a retry command.

## Identity and requirements

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Crate | `cargo-bumpp` |
| Direct binary | `bumpp` |
| Cargo subcommand | `cargo bumpp` |
| Minimum Rust version | 1.74 |
| Runtime tools | `cargo`, `git` |
| Dependencies | None in the published crate |
| License | MIT |

The tool is useful when the release unit is a local commit and tag. Registry publishing, changelog policy, credentials, and CI orchestration stay outside that unit.

## Install and learn

- [Getting started](/projects/cargo-bumpp/getting-started) — install and run safe first-release commands.
- [Architecture](/projects/cargo-bumpp/architecture) — follow the plan, rollback, git, and workspace stages.
- [Reference](/projects/cargo-bumpp/reference) — flags, release levels, exit codes, and configuration.
- [Workspace and rollback](/projects/cargo-bumpp/workspace-and-rollback) — shared versions, member versions, and failure recovery.
- [CI and release](/projects/cargo-bumpp/ci-and-release) — hand the tag to downstream automation.
- [Troubleshooting](/projects/cargo-bumpp/troubleshooting) — diagnose Git, signing, prompt, and workspace errors.
- [FAQ](/projects/cargo-bumpp/faq) — compare it with cargo-release and cargo-bump.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/imba97/cargo-bumpp) — Rust source, tests, and release workflow.

## Scope boundary

`cargo-bumpp` is a release preparation tool. It does not publish packages, generate changelogs, or provide a pull-request release workflow.

# cargo-bumpp architecture — plan, rollback, workspace, and git

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/architecture/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: cargo-bumpp builds a release plan from Cargo metadata, applies version changes, rolls back local failures, and pushes one explicit tag.

# cargo-bumpp architecture

The implementation is a small Rust CLI with no dependencies. It separates discovery and planning from mutation so the user can see what will change before the release point is created.

## Release pipeline

```text
arguments / selector
        │
        ▼
cargo metadata + git history ──► release plan
        │                              │
        │                         one confirmation
        ▼                              │
rewrite manifests + Cargo.lock ◄──────┘
        │
        ├─ git commit
        ├─ annotated tag
        └─ push branch + exact tag
```

## Workspace rules

The tool uses `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` to identify packages, shared workspace versions, and path dependencies. A workspace with one shared version can be bumped together. Independent member versions are reported rather than silently skipped; `--recursive` opts into bumping each member.

## Rollback boundary

If manifest writes, the commit, or tag creation fails, cargo-bumpp deletes the local tag, resets the release commit, and restores the file snapshot. A push is the first irreversible remote action. If it fails, the local commit and tag remain and the tool prints the exact retry command.

## Why no publish step?

The tag is a stable handoff point for CI. crates.io versions cannot be deleted or overwritten, so publishing is intentionally outside the one-command local transaction.

# cargo-bumpp CI and release — handing a tag to automation

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/ci-and-release/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: How cargo-bumpp fits into a CI release pipeline, what it intentionally stops before, and how to retry a failed remote push.

# cargo-bumpp CI and release

`cargo-bumpp` creates a local release point. A downstream CI workflow can treat the annotated tag as the handoff event for checks, packaging, and registry publication.

## Recommended handoff

```text
developer or release job
  └─ cargo bumpp --no-push   (inspect locally when needed)
       └─ commit + annotated tag
            └─ push branch + exact tag
                 └─ CI validates and publishes according to repository policy
```

The tool pushes the branch and the exact tag rather than every local tag. This avoids triggering a release workflow for unrelated tags in the same repository.

## What CI should own

- Running the project's tests and lint checks.
- Building release artifacts.
- Authenticating to crates.io or another registry.
- Publishing packages and creating release notes according to policy.
- Recording provenance and deployment status.

## What cargo-bumpp deliberately does not own

It does not publish to a registry, generate a changelog, or create a pull-request release flow. Those decisions require repository credentials and team policy that do not belong in a local version transaction.

## Push failure recovery

If the remote rejects the push, keep the local commit and tag. Read the printed Git error, fix the remote condition, and rerun the exact push command. If a tag must be moved to rerun a downstream workflow, use `cargo bumpp --retag [tag]` after inspecting the new target.

# cargo-bumpp FAQ — release flow, Cargo workspaces, and comparisons

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/faq/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: Answers to cargo-bumpp questions about publishing, changelogs, rollback, workspaces, retagging, and similar Cargo tools.

# cargo-bumpp FAQ

## Does cargo-bumpp publish to crates.io?

No. It stops at the commit and tag. CI can use that tag as the release trigger and own the registry credentials and publishing policy.

## Does it generate a changelog?

No. Changelog generation is deliberately outside the core bump → commit → tag → push path.

## How is it different from cargo-release?

`cargo-release` covers a broader publishing workflow and has more dependencies. `cargo-bumpp` focuses on a quick, interactive release point with zero dependencies and no registry publish step.

## How is it different from cargo-bump?

`cargo-bumpp` includes an interactive selector, shared workspace and path-dependency handling, a visible plan, rollback before push, commit and tag creation, and a retag flow.

## What does `conventional` do?

It reads the commit history since the previous reachable tag and chooses a major, minor, or patch level. The history window is capped by `--commit-window` (100 by default), and the command reports when it is truncated.

## What happens if push fails?

The local commit and tag remain. The tool prints git's error and a retry command because deleting local release state after a remote rejection would make recovery harder.

## Can I use it inside the cargo-bumpp repository?

Yes. The repository includes a dev-only Cargo alias so `cargo bumpp` can run the working tree. Outside a checkout, install the published crate or use `cargo install --path .`.

# cargo-bumpp getting started — install and run a release bump

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/getting-started/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: Install cargo-bumpp, run an interactive or explicit version bump, inspect the plan, and control commit, tag, and push behavior.

# Get started with cargo-bumpp

The default flow is intentionally visible: choose a version bump, inspect the plan, confirm once, and let the tool create the commit, tag, and targeted push.

## 1. Install

```bash
cargo install cargo-bumpp
```

This installs both `cargo bumpp` and the direct `bumpp` binary:

```bash
cargo bumpp --help
bumpp --help
```

Requirements are Rust 1.74 or newer, `cargo`, and `git` on `PATH`. Linux, macOS, and Windows are supported.

## 2. Run the first bump

Interactive selection:

```bash
cargo bumpp
```

Explicit patch release:

```bash
cargo bumpp patch
```

Preview a concrete version without pushing:

```bash
cargo bumpp 1.0.0 --no-push
```

Skip the final confirmation only when the surrounding automation already provides that guard:

```bash
cargo bumpp minor -y
```

## 3. Control the release boundary

Only update versions:

```bash
cargo bumpp --no-tag --no-push
```

Re-create and force-push the most recent tag when a downstream release workflow needs to run again:

```bash
cargo bumpp --retag
```

Use `--no-push` on a first run when you want to inspect the local commit and tag before any remote operation.

## 4. Know what happens on failure

Manifest and lockfile writes, the commit, and the tag are treated as one local transaction. A failure before push rolls the local state back. A push failure leaves the commit and tag in place and prints a retry command because the remote operation cannot be undone safely by the tool.

# cargo-bumpp reference — release levels, flags, and exit codes

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/reference/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: A factual cargo-bumpp reference for commands, release levels, flags, configuration precedence, and process exit codes.

# cargo-bumpp reference

## Invocation forms

```bash
cargo bumpp [release]
bumpp [release]
```

The Cargo subcommand and direct binary use the same release engine. A release can be selected interactively, named by level, or provided as an explicit version.

## Release values

`major`, `minor`, `patch`, `next`, `conventional`, `conventional-prerelease`, `premajor`, `preminor`, `prepatch`, `prerelease`, `as-is`, `prompt`, and concrete versions such as `1.2.3` are accepted. A version may be written with a leading `v`.

## High-value flags

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--release <level>` | Set the release level or version explicitly. |
| `--retag [tag]` | Re-create an existing tag and force-push it. |
| `--preid <id>` | Set the prerelease identifier; default is `beta`. |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the final confirmation. |
| `-p, --push` / `--no-push` | Enable or disable the remote push. |
| `-t, --tag [name]` / `--no-tag` | Create or skip the tag, optionally using a template. |
| `-c, --commit [message]` / `--no-commit` | Create or skip the release commit. |
| `-r, --recursive` | Bump independent workspace members too. |
| `--no-sign` | Override Git signing configuration for commit and tag. |
| `-x, --execute <command>` | Run a command after version writes and before commit. |
| `--current-version <version>` | Override automatic current-version detection. |
| `--print-commits` / `--no-print-commits` | Show or hide commits used by `conventional`. |
| `--lockfile` / `--no-lockfile` | Run or skip `cargo update --workspace`. |
| `--commit-window <n>` | Limit commits read by `conventional`; default 100. |
| `--configFilePath <path>` | Use another `bumpp.toml` path. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Print warnings and errors only. |

The short options intentionally follow the `bumpp` family: `-r` means recursive and `-p` means push.

## Configuration precedence

For supported settings, the effective order is command line, environment, `bumpp.toml`, then built-in defaults. Options that execute a command, such as `--execute`, must be supplied on the command line.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Completed successfully. |
| `1` | A check or release step failed; local state was restored where possible. |
| `2` | Usage or configuration error. |
| `130` | User cancelled at a prompt. |

# cargo-bumpp troubleshooting — Git, signing, prompts, and workspaces

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/troubleshooting/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: Resolve cargo-bumpp failures involving dirty worktrees, GPG signing, non-interactive terminals, workspace versions, and remote pushes.

# cargo-bumpp troubleshooting

## The working tree is not clean

The default Git check protects changes that are outside the planned release. Commit or stash first, or pass `--no-git-check` only when you accept that the release command is running with unrelated changes present.

## GPG signing blocks the release

Git configuration can enable commit or tag signing even when cargo-bumpp was not given `--sign`. If signing is not required for this release, pass `--no-sign`; if it is required, verify the key, agent, and PIN setup before retrying.

## The selector or confirmation cannot read input

Use an explicit release level in an interactive terminal, for example `cargo bumpp patch`. In automation, provide the level and `-y`, then keep the workflow's own approval gate before allowing a push.

## The workspace has different member versions

Read the plan's member list. If independent versions are intentional, use `--recursive`; if the workspace should share one version, normalize the manifests before running the bump.

## A push failed

The local commit and tag remain by design. Fix permissions, branch protection, remote history, or network access, then run the retry command printed by cargo-bumpp. Do not create a second bump just because the first push was rejected.

## A retag target is missing

Fetch tags first and verify the tag is reachable from the local repository:

```bash
git fetch --tags
cargo bumpp --retag v1.2.3 --no-push
```

The command must identify an existing tag before it can re-create or move it.

# cargo-bumpp workspace and rollback — versions, metadata, and recovery

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/projects/cargo-bumpp/workspace-and-rollback/
Language: en
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: How cargo-bumpp discovers Cargo workspace versions, handles path dependencies, and restores local state when a release step fails.

# cargo-bumpp workspace and rollback

## Metadata discovery

The tool reads `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` to learn package members, workspace versions, and path dependencies. It does not guess the project graph from filenames alone.

## Shared workspace versions

When members use a shared workspace version, one release level can update the shared package and dependency declarations together. The plan prints every affected manifest location so the user can inspect the exact change.

## Independent member versions

If several members carry different versions and the command is not recursive, cargo-bumpp reports the mismatch instead of silently skipping a member. `--recursive` opts into bumping members independently according to their own versions.

## Path dependency versions

Path dependencies can carry a version requirement that needs to move with the workspace release. The plan includes those changes, which is why reading Cargo metadata is part of the release design.

## Local transaction

The local stages are treated as one transaction:

```text
snapshot → write manifests/lockfile → commit → tag
    └─ failure before push → delete tag, reset commit, restore files
```

The push is outside the rollback boundary. A remote rejection does not erase the local release point; the user receives the exact retry command instead.

## Retagging

`--retag` is a separate operation. It re-creates an existing tag at the chosen commit and force-pushes that tag. It does not bump versions, write files, or create a new commit.

# cargo-bumpp — 交互式 Cargo 版本发布工具

URL: https://projects.imba97.dev/zh/projects/cargo-bumpp/
Language: zh-CN
Project: cargo-bumpp
Description: cargo-bumpp 是一个零依赖 Rust CLI，用于升级 Cargo 版本、更新 lockfile、提交、打 tag 和推送。

# cargo-bumpp

<p class="lead"><code>cargo-bumpp</code> 是一个面向 Cargo 项目的交互式、零依赖发布辅助工具。它选择或接收升级级别，更新清单与 <code>Cargo.lock</code>，展示计划，并在一次确认后提交、打 tag 和推送。</p>

维护者：[imba97](/zh/about)。

## 它解决什么问题？

它把常见的“升级 → 提交 → annotated tag → 推送”路径变成可见、可审阅的流程。工具止步于 tag，之后由 CI 负责发布 registry。

## 关键行为

| 行为 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 安装成本 | `cargo install cargo-bumpp`，没有运行期依赖。 |
| 版本输入 | 交互选择器、`major`、`minor`、`patch`、`conventional`、预发布级别或明确版本号。 |
| Workspace | 用 `cargo metadata` 识别共享版本和 path dependency，`--recursive` 才会分别升级成员。 |
| 安全边界 | 先展示改动，步骤 3–5 失败时回滚本地状态，推送失败时保留本地提交与 tag。 |
| 发布边界 | 只创建发布点，不发布 crates.io，也不创建 PR 流程。 |

## 发布模型

默认流程包含一次可见决策和六个阶段：

1. 选择升级级别或明确版本号。
2. 按模式读取 Cargo metadata 和 Git 历史。
3. 打印所有版本变化，包括清单路径和行号。
4. 一次确认后写入清单和 `Cargo.lock`。
5. 创建 release commit 和 annotated tag。
6. 推送分支与明确的 tag，除非使用 `--no-push`。

推送前的本地修改具备回滚能力。推送前失败会恢复工作树、提交和 tag；远端推送失败则保留本地发布点，并打印重试命令。

## 身份与要求

| 事实 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| crate | `cargo-bumpp` |
| 直接二进制 | `bumpp` |
| Cargo 子命令 | `cargo bumpp` |
| 最低 Rust 版本 | 1.74 |
| 运行期工具 | `cargo`、`git` |
| 依赖 | 发布 crate 没有依赖 |
| 许可证 | MIT |

它适合把本地 commit 和 tag 作为发布单元的项目；registry 发布、changelog、凭据和 CI 编排仍由外部流程负责。

- [架构](/zh/projects/cargo-bumpp/architecture)
